headline: **600,000** H200S
SIT IN HONG KONG
cover.hook_pick_reason: Leads with the 600,000 figure and the place, both stated on slide 1 and in the article's headline. The claim option (Beijing holds back) is also backed but the number-first version carries the same payload plus the concrete scale. The rivalry option frames it as Beijing versus Nvidia, which the article only implies. The 'under 200,000' option stays accurate only if read as conditional, and the cover has no room for 'could', so it is weaker. No reader-impact hook: the article states no effect on ordinary readers; the prices it gives are for China's unofficial server market and the stock charge concerns Nvidia.

slides.title: 600,000 H200s, stored in Hong Kong
body: About **600,000** Nvidia H200 AI chips are being stored in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports into mainland China, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar, as relayed by The Next Web.

slides.title: Beijing wants home-made chips
body: Beijing wants firms such as **Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek** to use Chinese-made chips instead, especially for inference, the step where a trained AI model answers users.

slides.title: Approvals could stay under 200,000
body: The total number of foreign chips China approves **could end up below 200,000**. Several big Chinese internet firms each received about 10,000 H200s in recent months, one source said.

slides.title: Servers cost triple on the grey market
body: By end of October, an eight-H200 server was offered on China's unofficial market for **more than 6m yuan**, about three times a year earlier. Blackwell servers, which the US bars from China, were offered for over 20m yuan.

slides.title: A tiny market, and a $400m charge
body: In its latest quarterly filing, Nvidia said H200 sales to China were **under 1%** of data centre revenue. It took a **$400m charge** for unsold H200 stock and purchase commitments.

facts.text: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are being stored in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports into mainland China, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar (as relayed by The Next Web).
Beijing wants firms such as Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to use Chinese-made chips instead, especially for inference.
The total number of foreign chips China approves could end up below 200,000; several big Chinese internet firms each received about 10,000 H200s in recent months, one source said.
By end of October an eight-H200 server was offered on China's unofficial market for more than 6m yuan, about three times a year earlier.
Servers with Blackwell chips, which the US does not allow to be sold to China, were offered for more than 20m yuan each.
In its latest quarterly filing Nvidia said H200 sales to China were under 1% of data centre revenue and it took a $400m charge for unsold H200 stock and purchase commitments.

sources.title: China holds back approval for Nvidia H200 chips stored in Hong Kong

caption:
About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are sitting in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports.

Reuters reported, citing two people familiar, as relayed by The Next Web. Beijing wants Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to use Chinese-made chips instead.

→ China's total approvals of foreign chips could end up below 200,000
→ An eight-H200 server was offered at more than 6m yuan by end of October, about 3x a year earlier
→ Nvidia's H200 sales to China were under 1% of data centre revenue, with a $400m charge

Who really controls the AI chip trade: Washington or Beijing?

Source: The Next Web, "China holds back approval for Nvidia H200 chips stored in Hong Kong", Nov 6, 2026.
